clue.text: Go back? That's the right way out!

parts.note: an egress is an exit, a way out of a place

explanation.surface: Someone heading back out through the exit declares that this is the proper route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the right way out!' reads as a cheerful exclamation, but it splits into right (R) and way out (EGRESS).
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to revert or move backwards to an earlier state.

clue.text: Said to be set down in the grass

indicators.note: the word for set down goes in the word for the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
to put something is to set it down

explanation.surface: Something is rumoured to have been laid in the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or supposed, as in 'reputed to be rich'.

clue.text: Refuse clothing over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone turns down clothes that are past their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish or waste, the noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: Charged over small transgressions

indicators.note: turned over means the word for charged is read backwards

parts.note: live describes a wire carrying electric charge

explanation.surface: Someone is prosecuted for some minor offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like a legal accusation, but it is the electrical sense, a live wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils are wicked acts or sins, which are transgressions.

clue.text: Living without Mike? There's a thought!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for living goes outside the letter for Mike

parts.note: sentient means alive and able to feel
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud about life without a friend called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'minus' but means outside, so M is inside SENTIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or opinion, a thought one holds or expresses.

clue.text: He throws an earthenware vessel

definitions.meaning: in baseball the player who throws the ball to the batter
a large jug for pouring liquids

explanation.definitionFit: Baseball's thrower and a jug for water share one name.

clue.text: Father seen before getting out of puff

indicators.note: the word for before is getting, taking in, the word for puff

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a puff is a piece of promotional writing, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A dad is spotted ahead of the rest, completely out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of puff' reads as breathless, but puff here is promotional copy, an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a title for a priest or chaplain, addressed as Father.

clue.text: Stand-in gets lock for siren

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker standing in for another
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An office substitute gets a curl of hair to play the seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alluring woman who leads men astray, a seductress.

clue.text: Run into student, first of intended victims

parts.note: to hit is to collide with, to run into
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
1ST is the short form of first, the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver strikes a student, the first of several planned targets.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit list names people marked out for attack or killing.

clue.text: Man in dreary assembly of old foreign forces

indicators.note: the letter for man goes inside the rearranged letters
an assembly puts parts together in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male or man

explanation.surface: A man sits in a gloomy gathering of veterans from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly of' rearranges DREARY to REDARY around M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Army was the army of the Soviet Union, foreign to the British setter and now historical.

clue.text: Tonic's taken in the right quantity

indicators.note: the tonic has taken in the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: a tonic is a medicinal drink, a potion; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A dose of medicine is swallowed in just the correct amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tonic's' is read as 'Tonic has', so POTION has taken in R.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a share or amount of something, a quantity of it.

clue.text: Thomas, in retreat during action, gets lowered status

indicators.note: Thomas's short form comes during, so inside, the word for an action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the name is read right to left

parts.note: Tom is the short form of Thomas

explanation.surface: A soldier called Thomas pulls back in battle and is busted down a rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' looks like the soldier's movement but reverses the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoted describes someone reduced to a lower rank, which is what Thomas gets in the surface.

clue.text: Happen to exhale

definitions.meaning: to come about or take place
to give off vapour through pores or leaves, as plants do

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to occur and, in botany, to breathe out moisture through the surface.

clue.text: Take in a bank somewhere in Germany

indicators.note: the abbreviation for take goes inside the word for a bank

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats
R is short for recipe, Latin for 'take', as written on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A financial institution gets taken over somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from the Latin recipe heading old prescriptions. 'Take in' looks like a phrasal verb meaning deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an old city on the Moselle in western Germany.

clue.text: Daughter hit hard and lived

parts.note: to welt is to beat or thrash, leaving weals

explanation.surface: A grim family story: a daughter was beaten, yet survived.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to reside or have one's home somewhere.

clue.text: Bully fell upon teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue, upon means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a fell is a hill in northern England; a tor is a rocky hill
a mentor is a trusted adviser or teacher

explanation.surface: A thug attacked a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell upon' reads as attacked, but fell is a hill (TOR), placed upon MENTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor harasses and persecutes others, as a bully does.

clue.text: Quick to adopt retreat with conviction

indicators.note: adopting takes something in, so the retreat goes inside the word for quick

parts.note: early can mean prompt or quick, ahead of time
a nest is a snug hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: Someone eager to embrace a withdrawal acts in deadly seriousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking earnestly means speaking sincerely and seriously, with real conviction.

clue.text: Soldiers bound to knock road safety device

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
to dart is to dash or bound
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: Troops are certain to criticise a piece of traffic safety equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to knock' reads as 'certain to criticise'; bound is DART and knock is RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A radar trap is a speed check using radar to catch speeding drivers.

clue.text: Treated fairly and informed about energy price

indicators.note: the word for informed goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to have told someone is to have informed them
E is the physics symbol for energy
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A customer says they were dealt with fairly and kept up to date on their energy tariff.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tolerated someone is to have put up with them, allowing them fair room.

clue.text: Newspaper bill? See identification!

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A demand for payment, with a request to show papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a small-format popular newspaper.

clue.text: Type of oil processed in Leeds

indicators.note: processed means changed by treatment, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of oil is refined in a northern English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed oil is pressed from flax seeds and used in paints and varnishes.

clue.text: Delightful meal without papa

indicators.note: without means the letter for papa is taken out

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely dinner where Dad was absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Sharpen tack outside radio programme

indicators.note: the word for tack goes outside the word for sharpen

parts.note: a pin is a tack
to hone is to sharpen a blade

explanation.surface: Instructions for sharpening a tack outdoors on a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone-in is a broadcast where listeners call in to speak on air.

clue.text: Odd desire to store uranium waste

indicators.note: storing keeps something inside, so the letter for uranium goes in
odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A strange urge to stockpile nuclear fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges DESIRE to RESIDE, with U stored inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after a process, leftover waste.

clue.text: Crooner has energy for a lot of drinking

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the famous American crooner
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A singer with plenty of vigour goes in for heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excessive indulgence, especially a drinking spree.

clue.text: Trustworthy girl gets many promises of money

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
IOUs are written promises to pay, so the plural

explanation.surface: A reliable young woman collects a pile of pledges of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracious means truthful, habitually telling the truth, so someone who can be relied on.

clue.text: Six settle for excursion

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to sit is to settle into a seat

explanation.surface: Half a dozen people settle on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit is a trip to see a person or place, a short excursion.

clue.text: Length of string

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch
a series or sequence of linked things

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a surveyor's measure of 22 yards and also a linked series, such as a string of shops.

clue.text: Classical matricide finds drug in fashion stores

indicators.note: the letter for the drug is put inside the rearranged word
to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A notorious mother-killer turns up narcotics in clothing shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges STORES into ORESTS, then E goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Orestes avenged his father Agamemnon by killing his mother Clytemnestra.

clue.text: Romeo earned beaten backside

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: beaten means knocked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lover gets the spanking he deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' looks like the punishment but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear end is the back part of something, and colloquially the buttocks.

clue.text: Enlightened philosopher managed European corruption

parts.note: to have done something is to have managed it
rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A wise thinker coped with decadence across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot, editor of the Encyclopédie, was a leading philosopher of the French Enlightenment.

clue.text: Coppers brought about an act of self-punishment

indicators.note: the word for coppers goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: pence are copper coins in Britain, called coppers

explanation.surface: Police officers brought about some act of self-inflicted suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police but means copper coins, British pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is a voluntary act of mortification undertaken to atone for sin.
